library(ggplot2)

# Exercises

## Exercise 2

Using the `datasets::trees` data, complete the following. This question refreshes create a linear model, graphing the linear model, and introduces using some LaTeX expressions on the graph.

**a)** Create a regression model for $y=$ `Volume` as a function of $x=$ `Height`.

```{r}
data('trees', package = 'datasets')

model.trees <- lm(Volume ~ Height, data = trees) 
```

After importing the trees data from the "datasets" package in R, I created a regression model for Volume as a function of Height.

**b)** Display the `summary` of the  model to view the y-intercept and slope of the regression line.

```{r}
summary(model.trees)
```

Using the summary() function, we can view the y-intercept and slope of the regression sign.

**c)** Using `ggplot2`, create a scatter plot of Volume vs Height. 

```{r}
ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume)) + 
  geom_point()
```

Using ggplot, I graphed a scatter plot of Volume vs. Height.

**d)** Color the scatter using the `Girth` variable.

```{r}
ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) + 
  geom_point()
```

Next, I colored the points of the scatter plot using the Girth variable.

**e)** Modify the color scheme using a RColorBrewer palette.

```{r}
ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral")
```

Next, I changed the color scheme to the RColorBrewer palette "Spectral".

**f)** Create a nice white filled rectangle to add text information. The following might be useful.

```{r}
ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral") + 
  annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74,
         fill='white', color='black')
```

Next, I added a white text box using annotate() to display future text.

**g)** Use the `broom` package to extract the coefficients of the best-fit line. Add this information as an annotation to the graph, which should follow a form that looks like $\hat{y}_i = (INTERCEPT) + (SLOPE)* x_i$. Place the annotation within the white text box.

```{r}
tidy(model.trees)

ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral") + 
  annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74,
         fill='white', color='black') + 
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$\\hat{y}_i = (-87.12361) + (1.54335)* x_i$"), 
         x = 70, y = 67, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3')
```

Next, after extracting the coefficients of the best-fit line, I added the y-intercept and slope information as an annotation to the graph within the white box.

**h)** Use the `broom` package to extract the coefficient of determination $r^2$ from the model. Add the annotation to your graph, which should look something like $R^2 = (VALUE)$

```{r}
glance(model.trees)

ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral") + 
  annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74,
           fill='white', color='black') + 
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$\\hat{y}_i = (-87.12361) + (1.54335)* x_i$"), 
           x = 70, y = 70, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3') +
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$R^2 = (0.3579026)$"),
           x = 70, y = 64, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3')
```

Next, after extracting the coefficient of determination from the regression model, I added the R-squared value as an annotation to the graph also within the white box.

**i)** Add the regression line in red. There are several ways to do this.

```{r}
trees <- augment(model.trees, trees, interval='confidence')
trees <- trees %>% select(c("Girth", "Height", "Volume", ".fitted"))
head(trees)

ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(y = .fitted), color = "red") +
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral") + 
  annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74,
           fill='white', color='black') + 
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$\\hat{y}_i = (-87.12361) + (1.54335)* x_i$"), 
           x = 70, y = 70, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3') +
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$R^2 = (0.3579026)$"),
           x = 70, y = 64, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3')
```

First, I used augment to add the regression model information to our original data frame and then selected the original columns and the .fitted column. Next, I plotted the same scatter plot from above, but added a geom_text() layer for the regression line in red.

**j)** Properly label the axes of the graph.

```{r}
ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(y = .fitted), color = "red") +
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral") + 
  annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74,
           fill='white', color='black') + 
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$\\hat{y}_i = (-87.12361) + (1.54335)* x_i$"), 
           x = 70, y = 70, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3') +
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$R^2 = (0.3579026)$"),
           x = 70, y = 64, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3') +
  labs(x = "Height (ft)", y = "Volume (cubic ft)", color = "Girth (in)")
```

Next, I labeled the axes and color legend of the graph using labs().

**k)** Add a descriptive title to the graph.

```{r}
ggplot(data = trees,
       aes(x = Height, y = Volume, color = Girth)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(y = .fitted), color = "red") +
  scale_colour_continuous(palette = "Spectral") + 
  annotate('rect', xmin=65, xmax=75, ymin=60, ymax=74,
           fill='white', color='black') + 
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$\\hat{y}_i = (-87.12361) + (1.54335)* x_i$"), 
           x = 70, y = 70, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3') +
  annotate("text", label = TeX("$R^2 = (0.3579026)$"),
           x = 70, y = 64, size = 3.3, color = 'grey3') +
  labs(title = "Black Cherry Tree Volume vs. Height with Best-Fit Line and R^2 Value",
       x = "Height (ft)", y = "Volume (cubic ft)", color = "Girth (in)")
```

Lastly, I added a descriptive title to the graph within the labs() layer.
